newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Band B charges to guide Telebras rates. [CORRECTED 17:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Band B charges to guide Telebras rates. [CORRECTED 17:20 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects headline to reflect fact that Telebras does not operate Band B services.)
Brazil's Telebras will adjust its cellular telephone rates to be competitive with those set by new private B Band operators due to come on stream late this year and in 1998, a company official said.
"We're in a different scenario now. We have to be competitive," a spokesman for Telebras told Reuters.
"Telebras will use B Band rates in different areas as points of reference," he added.

Consortia that win concessions to operate on the B Band frequency are expected to aggressively seek to carve out market shares in Brazil, in part by adopting lower rates than those now charged by Telebras's state-level subsidiaries.

Last week, Canada-led Americel group became the first consortium to win a B Band contract, bidding 338.5 million reais, some 25.4 percent above the base price, for an area covering central and western Brazil, including Brasilia.
The government, which received bids on eight of the nine other concession areas nationwide, is expected to award the remaining licenses in the next two months.

A local newspaper quoted Telebras President Fernando Xavier Ferreira as saying Telebras would adopt the same rates as those offered by B Band operators but a spokesman denied that, saying B Band rates would only be used as a guide.
"Americel's proposal and the proposals of other B Band operators will be used as a point of reference only," he said.
The Brazilian government plans to break up and privatize Telebras, beginning with its Sao Paulo unit Telesp and long-distance monopoly Embratel, in early 1998.
